core_obligations: Reduce to a single prime and exponent (proof lines 16079-16088): write F as a direct sum of sheaves F_i annihilated by prime powers; the additivity lemma reduces the theorem to each summand, so one may assume that l^n annihilates F for a prime l and n > 0.

Reduce to an extension by zero from a dense open (proof lines 16089-16099): constructibility gives a dense open U over which F is of finite type and locally constant; since dim X <= 1 one may shrink U so that it is a disjoint union of irreducible subschemes, and the restriction lemma reduces to F = j_!G with G a finite type locally constant sheaf on U, annihilated by l^n.

Split into the irreducible components (proof lines 16101-16113): for U = U_1 coproduct ... coproduct U_n with U_i irreducible, the extension by zero decomposes as the direct sum of the j_{i!}(G|U_i), and each of those is handled by the companion lemma for an irreducible open; hence finiteness holds, and with it the two assertions of the statement.
proof_roadmap: Split the coefficient sheaf into prime-power torsion summands and use additivity of finiteness.
Reduce to the extension by zero of a finite type locally constant sheaf from a dense open, made a disjoint union of irreducible pieces by dimension one.
difficulty_reason: The theorem establishes finiteness of the cohomology of a torsion constructible sheaf of Lambda-modules on a separated curve over an algebraically closed field, in the prime-to-characteristic case and in the proper case (statement lines 16061-16076). The proof (proof lines 16078-16113) decomposes the sheaf into prime-power torsion summands, reduces by the additivity lemma to a single such summand, reduces to the extension by zero of a finite type locally constant sheaf from a dense open which dimension one lets one split into irreducible pieces, and applies the irreducible case componentwise. H2: a chain of standard reductions, each written out.
